nota: Words of this language that look borrowed from another language but do not exist there with that meaning, grouped by the language they imitate.

parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دائمی (daimî), from Classical Persian دائمی (dā'imī / dâ'emi), a pseudo-Arabism from the root د و م (d w m).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فیات (fiyat), فیئات (fiʼat, “price”). Pseudo-Arabism formed artificially in Ottoman by combining the Arabic plural ending ـَات (-āt) with فی (fi, “rate, price”), itself
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish هائله (hâʼile), a pseudo-Arabism from Arabic هَائِلة (hāʔila), inflected form of Arabic هَائِل (hāʔil), from هَالَ (hāla, “to frighten”).

parole.significato: Mahya lights (decorative lights strung up between the minarets of Turkish mosques to form illuminated words or pictures…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ماهیه (mahiyye, “monthly (pay or allowance)”), pseudo-Arabism from Persian ماه (māh / mâh, “month”) + Arabic ـِيَّة (-iyya).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish معند (muʼannid), a pseudo-Arabism derived from Arabic عَنَدَ (ʕanada) as a Form II active participle.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ملحم (mülahham), a Pseudo-Arabism, derived from لَحُمَ (laḥuma, “to be fleshy or corpulent”), as a Form II active participle.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تنقید (tenkid), from Classical Persian تَنْقِید (tanqīd), a pseudo-Arabism from the root ن ق د (n q d).

parole.significato: basket (basketball: act of putting the ball through the basket)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English basket. The sense "basketball" is a pseudo-anglicism derived from an ellipsis of English basketball, borrowed from French basket.
From Ottoman Turkish بوقس (boks), from French boxe, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English boxing.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English holding company.
Borrowed from French auto-stop, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from auto- (relating to cars) + stop (hitchiking).
Borrowed from French smoking, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English smoking jacket.
Borrowed from French sweat, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English sweatshirt.
